subject: Inset width/length limit with lage dataset using nodepie

messages.author: 3f98c2cb066b2e7d
messages.subject: Inset width/length limit with lage dataset using nodepie
parts:
Hello,

I used to be able to generate trees with 300+ taxa with pie charts mapped over 200 nodes using nodepies. One of the recent updates (I could not figure out which one) seems to limit the possible downscaling of pie charts using the width and length option of inset.

In the following examples, changing the values for width and length does not affect the size of the pie chart:

> set,seed(1)
> tr <- rtree(100)
>p <- ggtree(tr)
>pie <- nodepie(p$data, cols = 4:5)
>inset (p, pie, width=1, height=1)
>inset (p, pie, width=0.5, height=0.5)
Both these insets works and generate smaller pies for second tree.


>inset (p, pie, width=0.2, height =0.2)
Generates the tree with no pies. 

Is there a way of extending the limits of the downscaling of the pies for large datasets? 

Cordially,

 Ludo
